# {{< fa user-clock size=1x >}} &nbsp;&nbsp;Exercise 2 (20 min)


## Exercise 2 

#### **Part 1**: Merge herbarium and GBIF data

> Remember Excercise 1 : our goal is to complete the herbarium data with extra field observations from GBIF.
> We downloaded both datasets, but before we can merge them together, we need to homogenize column names and make sure the column contents are compatible (format, units, etc).

* Load the herbarium data and the GBIF occurrences into R and inspect the formats. What needs to be cleaned ? <br/>

 > {{< fa lightbulb >}} &nbsp; To convert latitude coordinates from DMS (Days Minutes Seconds) to decimal degrees, use the `parzer::parse_lat()` function.

<br/>

#### **Part 2**: Plot the combined observations on a map

* Use the `sf` pacakge to transform the datapoints into an sf object.
> {{< fa lightbulb >}} &nbsp; Use the 4326 projection as coordinate refence system (crs).

* Use the `mapview` package to produce an interactive map and vizalise the plant occurrences. What can you see ?

* Bonus question : instead of `mapview`, use the `rnaturalearth` package combined with `ggplot`, and export the map.






## Correction part 1


```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true

## Load GBIF occurrences ----
occ <- read.csv2("../gbif_occurrences.csv")

## Load herbarium data ----
df <- read.csv2("../herbier_gbif.csv")

## Harmonize column names
df <- df |> janitor::clean_names()
occ <- occ |> janitor::clean_names()

```

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

## Load GBIF occurrences ----
occ <- read.csv2("gbif_occurrences.csv")

## Load herbarium data ----
df <- read.csv2("herbier_gbif.csv")

## Harmonize column names
df <- df |> janitor::clean_names()
occ <- occ |> janitor::clean_names()

```

<br/>

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true

## Herbarium data : remove columns we don't need and focus on the 2 selected species ----
df2 <- df |> 
  dplyr::select(country_col, full_name, lat, lon) |>
  dplyr::filter(full_name %in% c("Catopsis sessiliflora", "Catopsis nutans"))

## Check
str(df2)
```

 > The herbarium dataset structure and column names are OK, but latitude and longitude are not consistent : coordinates are somtimes in DMS format (degree - minutes - seconds, e.g. 5° 35' 12\" N) instead of decimal degrees (e.g. 17.3187987).




## Correction part 1

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true

## The parzer package converts them automatically ----
df2$lat <- parzer::parse_lat(df2$lat) 
df2$lon <- parzer::parse_lon(df2$lon) 

str(df2)
```

> Success !

Now inspect GBIF dataset:

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true

## GBIF occurrences: clean species names so they are consistent with the herbarium ones----
occ$scientific_name <- stringr::str_replace_all(occ$scientific_name, "Catopsis sessiliflora.*", "Catopsis sessiliflora")
occ$scientific_name <- stringr::str_replace_all(occ$scientific_name, "Catopsis nutans.*", "Catopsis nutans")

## Rename and reorder column names ----
occ <- dplyr::rename(occ, full_name = scientific_name, lat = decimal_latitude, lon = decimal_longitude) 
occ <- occ[,c(4, 1, 2, 3)]
df2 <- dplyr::rename(df2, country = country_col)

## Check ----
colnames(occ) == colnames(df2)

```


```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true

## Append herbarium and GBIf occurrences ----
tab <- rbind(df2, occ)

```


## Correction part 2


```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true

## Convert occurrences into sf object ----
tab_sf <- tab |> 
  sf::st_as_sf(
    coords = c("lon", "lat"),
    crs = 4326 
  )

## Plot map with mapview ----
mapview::mapview(tab_sf, map.types = "OpenStreetMap.Mapnik", zcol = "full_name")

```




## Correction part 2 bonus

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

## Choose countries you want to see ----
world <- rnaturalearth::ne_countries()
gtm <- rnaturalearth::ne_countries(country = "Guatemala")
gtm_clb <- rnaturalearth::ne_countries(country = c("Guatemala", "Colombia"))
americas <- rnaturalearth::ne_countries(continent = c("North America", "South America"))

## Plot map ----
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = gtm_clb)  +
  geom_sf(data = tab_sf, mapping = aes(color = full_name)) +
  theme_minimal()
```
